label: assumption_null_cone_foliation
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{assumption_null_cone_foliation}
We assume that there exists an open causal diamond $\mathsf{D} = I^+(p_-) \cap I^-(p_+)$ generated by two points $p_-, p_+ \in \mathcal{M}$, such that the following holds. There is a smooth future-directed timelike curve $\gamma \colon I \to \mathsf{D}$,
and an open neighbourhood $M$ of $K$ such that
\[
  K \subset M \Subset \mathsf{D},
  \qquad
  \overline{M} \cap \gamma(I) = \emptyset.
\]
For every $\tau \in I$, the \emph{regular part} of the future null
cone of $\gamma(\tau)$,
\[
  \mathcal{H}_\tau
  =
  \bigl(\partial J^+(\gamma(\tau)) \setminus \{\gamma(\tau)\}\bigr)
  \cap \mathsf{D},
\]
is a smooth null hypersurface, and the family
$\{\mathcal{H}_\tau\}_{\tau \in I}$ forms a smooth foliation of
\begin{equation}
    \label{def_of_dgamma}
\mathsf{D}_\gamma=\mathsf{D} \setminus \gamma(I).
\end{equation}
More precisely,
\[
  \mathsf{D}_\gamma = \bigsqcup_{\tau \in I} \mathcal{H}_\tau.
\]
and there exists a smooth function $f \colon \mathsf{D}_\gamma
\to I$ with $df \neq 0$ such that $\mathcal{H}_\tau = f^{-1}(\tau)$
for all $\tau \in I$.
head: environment
name: Null-cone foliation

title: Remark
body_md:
Let us comment briefly on the geometric content of
Assumption~\ref{assumption_null_cone_foliation}.
The inclusion
\begin{equation}
    K \subset M \Subset \mathsf{D}
\end{equation}
ensures that the compact set $K$ is contained in a relatively compact
causal diamond. In particular, all the geometric constructions below
can be carried out in a fixed causally bounded region.

The condition $\overline{M}\cap\gamma(I)=\emptyset$
ensures that the neighborhood in which we work stays uniformly away
from the vertices of the null cones. This allows us to disregard the
singular behavior of the cones at their vertices.
For each $\tau\in I$, the set $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ is assumed to be a smooth null hypersurface. This is not automatic on a
general Lorentzian manifold: null cones may develop conjugate points
and caustics, and their causal boundaries need not be smooth globally.
Thus, this condition amounts to assuming that the relevant portions of
the null cones are free of such singularities in $\mathsf{D}$.
head: environment

label: rem_D_globhyp
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem_D_globhyp}
The causal diamond $\mathsf{D}=I^+(p_-)\cap I^-(p_+)$ is globally
hyperbolic. It is causally convex: if $x,y\in\mathsf{D}$ and
$\lambda$ is a future-directed causal curve from $x$ to $y$, then
for any $z$ on $\lambda$ one has $p_-\ll x\leq z$, hence $p_-\ll z$,
and $z\leq y\ll p_+$, hence\footnote{This uses the chronological transitivity property: $x \ll y$ and $y \leq z$ implies $x \ll z$.}$z\ll p_+$, so $z\in\mathsf{D}$. For $x,y\in\mathsf{D}$, the diamond $J^+(x)\cap J^-(y)$ in
$\mathsf{D}$ equals the one in $\mathcal{M}$
hence is compact. As a consequence $\mathsf{D}$ is globally hyperbolic.
head: environment

label: def_extension
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def_extension}
A null-cone extension of $(M,g)$ is a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold $(\mathcal{M},\tilde g)$ of dimension $1+n$, together with an isometric, time-orientation preserving embedding $\overlineM\subset\mathcal{M}$, such that Assumption~\ref{assumption_null_cone_foliation} holds for $(\mathcal{M},\tilde g)$ and some compact set $K\subsetM$, with $M$ as the neighbourhood of $K$.
head: environment
name: Null-cone extension

label: thm_calderon
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm_calderon}
Assume that $(M,g)$ has a null-cone extension. Let $q_1,q_2\in C_0^\infty(M)$. If $\mathcal C_{q_1}(M)\subset\mathcal C_{q_2}(M)$, then $q_1=q_2$.
head: environment

label: rem_conformal
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem_conformal}
For $n\ge2$, Theorem~\ref{thm_calderon} also recovers positive conformal factors $c$ inside $M$ by the same gauge transformation as in \cite[Section~1]{alexakis2022}. Let $c_1,c_2$ be positive conformal factors with $c_j=1$ near $\partialM$, and assume that the Cauchy data set of $\Box_{c_1g}$ on $M$ is contained in that of $\Box_{c_2g}$. The map $u\mapsto c_j^{(n-1)/4}u$ sends the solutions of $\Box_{c_jg}u=0$ to those of $(\Box_g+q_j)w=0$, where
\[
q_j=-c_j^{-(n-1)/4}\,\Box_g\,c_j^{(n-1)/4}\in C_0^\infty(M),
\]
and it does not change the Cauchy data on $\partialM$. Hence $\mathcal C_{q_1}(M)\subset\mathcal C_{q_2}(M)$, and Theorem~\ref{thm_calderon} gives $q_1=q_2$. Then $v=c_1^{(n-1)/4}-c_2^{(n-1)/4}\in C_0^\infty(M)$ solves $(\Box_g+q_1)v=0$, so $v=0$ by uniqueness for the Cauchy problem, and we obtain $c_1=c_2$.
head: environment

label: assumption_sources
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{assumption_sources}
We assume that $\chi\in C^\infty_c(\mathsf{D}_\gamma; [0,1])$ satisfies the following. For every $x\in K$ the segment of the null generator through $x$ from $\gamma(f(x))$ to $x$ meets $\{\chi>0\}$.
head: environment
name: the sources

label: thm_main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm_main}
There is $C>0$, depending only on $A$ in~\eqref{def_of_admissible} and on the geometric quantities of Assumption~\ref{assumption_null_cone_foliation} such that for all admissible $q_1,q_2$
\[
\|q_1-q_2\|_{L^2(K)}\le C\mathcal E.
\]
In particular, if $(\mathcal Lq_1)_\tau=(\mathcal Lq_2)_\tau$ for almost every $\tau\in I$, then $q_1=q_2$.

label: lem_carleman_eq
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem_carleman_eq}
Let $U\subset\mathcal{M}$ be open and $\ell, \lambda,v$ be smooth real valued functions on $U$. Then, in $U$,
\begin{align*}
\tfrac12\bigl|e^\ell\Box_g(e^{-\ell}v)\bigr|^2
&= Q_+(\nabla v) + Q_-(\nabla\ell)v^2 + \operatorname{div}(B) + R \\
&\quad + \tfrac12\bigl|(\Delta_g+q_\ell+\lambda)v\bigr|^2 + \tfrac12\bigl|(S_\ell+\lambda)v\bigr|^2,
\end{align*}
where, writing $a=\lambda-\Delta_g\ell$,
\[
Q_\pm(X)=2D^2\ell(X,X)\pm a\,G(X), \qquad q_\ell = G(\nabla\ell)-\Delta_g\ell, \qquad S_\ell = 2\nabla\ell,
\]
\[
B = -\bigl((S_\ell+\lambda)v\bigr)\nabla v + \bigl(G(\nabla v)-(q_\ell+\lambda)v^2\bigr)\nabla\ell + \tfrac12 v^2\nabla\lambda,
\]
\[
R = \bigl(\operatorname{div}(a\nabla\ell) - a\lambda - \tfrac12\Delta_g\lambda\bigr)v^2.
\]
head: environment

label: lem_algebra
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We write $Z = s Y_1 + Z'$ where $g(Y_1, Z') = 0$, and consider
\[
\tilde Z = 2 g(Z, Y_1) Z - g(Z, Z) Y_1.
\]
Observe that \eqref{abs_nonpos} is equivalent to $g(\tilde Z, Y_2) \ge 0$.

The case $Z = 0$ is trivial. Let us assume that $Z \ne 0$. We have
\begin{align*}
g(\tilde Z, Y_1)
&= 2 g(Z, Y_1)^2 - g(Z, Z) g(Y_1, Y_1)\\
&= 2 s^2 g(Y_1, Y_1)^2 - \bigl(s^2 g(Y_1, Y_1) + g(Z', Z')\bigr) g(Y_1, Y_1)\\
&= s^2 g(Y_1, Y_1)^2 - g(Z', Z') g(Y_1, Y_1) > 0,
\end{align*}
since $Z'$ is spacelike due to the orthogonality $g(Y_1, Z') = 0$, and since $s \ne 0$ or $Z' \ne 0$ due to $Z \ne 0$. In particular, $\tilde Z \ne 0$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{z_causal}
\begin{aligned}
g(\tilde Z, \tilde Z)
&= 4 g(Z, Y_1)^2 g(Z, Z) - 4 g(Z, Y_1)^2 g(Z, Z) + g(Z, Z)^2 g(Y_1, Y_1)\\
&= g(Z, Z)^2 g(Y_1, Y_1) \le 0.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Thus $\tilde Z$ is causal. By $g(\tilde Z, Y_1) > 0$ the vectors $Y_1$ and $\tilde Z$ lie in opposite timecones, as do $Y_2$ and $\tilde Z$, since $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ lie in the same timecone. Hence $g(\tilde Z, Y_2) \ge 0$.

It remains to consider the case $g(\tilde Z, Y_2) = 0$. As $\tilde Z$ and $Y_2$ are causal, the orthogonality implies that $Y_2$ is null and $\tilde Z = aY_2$ for some $a \in \mathbb R \setminus 0$. Hence $Z$ is null due to \eqref{z_causal}. As \eqref{abs_nonpos} holds with equality and $Z$ is null, we have
\[
g(Z, Y_1) g(Z, Y_2) = 0.
\]
As $Y_1$ is timelike and $Z$ is null, we have $g(Z, Y_1) \ne 0$. Hence $g(Z, Y_2) = 0$. As both $Z$ and $Y_2$ are null, there is $c \ne 0$ such that $Z = cY_2$.

label: lem_stokes
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem_stokes}
Let $X=\overline Q\cap\overlineM$ be as in Section~\ref{sec_setup}, and let $\nu$ be the outer unit $h$-normal of $M$ along $\Gamma$. Then for every smooth vector field $B$ on $X$,
\[
\int_{Q\capM}\operatorname{div}_g(B)\,dV \;=\; -\int_{\mathcal H\cap\overlineM}\frac{\langle B,d\varphi\rangle}{|\nabla_h\varphi|_h}\,d\sigma_h \;+\; \int_\Gamma h(B,\nu)\,d\sigma_h^\Gamma .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Section~\ref{sec_setup}, $X$ is a compact manifold with corners and $\partial X=(\mathcal H\cap\overlineM)\cup\Gamma$. Since $dV_g=dV_h$, we have $\operatorname{div}_g(B)\,dV_g=d(\iota_B\,dV_h)$. Stokes' theorem on $X$  is valid on manifolds with corners~\cite{lee2002} and gives
\[
\int_X\operatorname{div}_g(B)\,dV_g=\int_{\partial X}\iota_B\,dV_h .
\]

On each of the two smooth pieces of $\partial X$, let $\eta$ be the outer unit $h$-normal. Thus $\eta=\nu$ on $\Gamma$, and $\eta=\nu_{\mathcal H}:=-\nabla_h\varphi/|\nabla_h\varphi|_h$ on $\mathcal H$, since $X\subset\{\varphi\ge0\}$. Write $B=h(B,\eta)\,\eta+B^{\tan}$, with $B^{\tan}$ tangent to the boundary. Let $e_1,\dots,e_n$ be an $h$-orthonormal frame of the boundary, positively oriented with respect to the boundary orientation. Then $(\eta,e_1,\dots,e_n)$ is $h$-orthonormal and positively oriented, so
\[
dV_h(\eta,e_1,\dots,e_n)=1=d\sigma_h(e_1,\dots,e_n).
\]
Since $dV_h$ is alternating and $B^{\tan}$ is tangential, $dV_h(B^{\tan},e_1,\dots,e_n)=0$. Hence
\[
(\iota_B\,dV_h)(e_1,\dots,e_n)=dV_h(B,e_1,\dots,e_n)=h(B,\eta),
\]
that is, $\iota_B\,dV_h=h(B,\eta)\,d\sigma_h$ on each piece. This gives the formula, since on $\mathcal H$
\[
h(B,\nu_{\mathcal H})=-\frac{h(B,\nabla_h\varphi)}{|\nabla_h\varphi|_h}=-\frac{\langle B,d\varphi\rangle}{|\nabla_h\varphi|_h}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove the estimate with $\Box_gu$ in place of $Pu$, and for real valued $u$. Since $\Box_g$ is real, this estimate then holds for complex valued $u$, by applying it to $\operatorname{Re}u$ and $\operatorname{Im}u$. Constants $c,C>0$ do not depend on $\sigma$, $u$ or $\tau$, and may change from line to line. All pointwise bounds below are obtained from continuous functions on the compact set $\overlineM$.


\medskip\noindent
\textbf{1. The bulk terms.}
Fix $\mu,\delta>0$ with $|D^2\psi(Z,Z)|\le\mu|Z|_h^2$ and $|G(\nabla\psi)|\ge\delta$ on $\overlineM$. Let $\zeta\ge\zeta_0$, with $\zeta_0$ fixed below, and set $\tilde\psi=e^{\zeta\psi}$ and $\ell=\sigma\tilde\psi$. Then $\nabla\ell=\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\,\nabla\psi$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq_hess_ell}
D^2\ell(Z,Z)=\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\bigl(D^2\psi(Z,Z)+\zeta\,g(\nabla\psi,Z)^2\bigr).
\end{equation}
Let $v=e^\ell u$, $a=\sigma\zeta^2\delta\tilde\psi$ and $\lambda=a+\Delta_g\ell$. Lemma~\ref{lem_carleman_eq} with $U=Q\capM$, without its two squares, gives
\begin{equation}\label{star}
Q_+(\nabla v)+Q_-(\nabla\ell)\,v^2\le\tfrac12\bigl|e^\ell\Box_gu\bigr|^2-\operatorname{div}(B)-R .
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq_hess_ell},
\[
Q_+(Z)=2\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\,D^2\psi(Z,Z)+2\sigma\zeta^2\tilde\psi\bigl(g(\nabla\psi,Z)^2+\tfrac\delta2G(Z)\bigr).
\]
Write $Z=s\nabla\psi+Z'$ with $g(\nabla\psi,Z')=0$; then $Z'$ is spacelike and
\[
g(\nabla\psi,Z)^2+\tfrac\delta2G(Z)=s^2|G(\nabla\psi)|\bigl(|G(\nabla\psi)|-\tfrac\delta2\bigr)+\tfrac\delta2G(Z')\ge\tfrac{\delta^2}2s^2+\tfrac\delta2G(Z'),
\]
which yields $Q_+(Z)\ge2\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\,(\zeta c-\mu)\,|Z|_h^2$.
Since $G(\nabla\ell)<0$, we have $-a\,G(\nabla\ell)\ge0$, and
\[
Q_-(\nabla\ell)\ge2D^2\ell(\nabla\ell,\nabla\ell)=2\sigma^3\zeta^3\tilde\psi^3\bigl(D^2\psi(\nabla\psi,\nabla\psi)+\zeta\,G(\nabla\psi)^2\bigr)\ge2\sigma^3\zeta^3\tilde\psi^3\bigl(\zeta\delta^2-\mu|\nabla\psi|_h^2\bigr).
\]
Taking $\zeta_0$ large enough, both brackets are positive on $\overlineM$ for $\zeta\ge\zeta_0$. Moreover $a$, $\lambda$ and $\nabla\ell$ are $O(\sigma)$. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq_bulk}
Q_+(Z)\ge c\sigma|Z|_h^2,\qquad Q_-(\nabla\ell)\ge c\sigma^3,\qquad |R|\le C\sigma^2v^2\qquad\text{on }\overlineM .
\end{equation}
Integrating \eqref{star} over $Q\capM$, using Lemma~\ref{lem_stokes} and \eqref{eq_bulk}, and absorbing $C\sigma^2\|v\|^2_Q$ for $\sigma_0$ large enough,
\begin{equation}\label{eq_integrated}
c\sigma\|\nabla_h v\|^2_Q+c\sigma^3\|v\|^2_Q-\int_{\mathcal H\cap\overlineM}\frac{\langle B,d\varphi\rangle}{|\nabla_h\varphi|_h}\,d\sigma_h\le\tfrac12\|e^\ell\Box_gu\|^2_Q+\Bigl|\int_\Gamma h(B,\nu)\,d\sigma_h^\Gamma\Bigr| .
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{2. The boundary terms.}
With $\beta:=\Delta_g\tilde\psi$ and $\Upsilon:=\zeta^2\delta\tilde\psi+\beta$, we have $\lambda=\sigma\Upsilon$, $q_\ell+\lambda=\sigma^2\zeta^2\tilde\psi^2G(\nabla\psi)+\sigma\zeta^2\delta\tilde\psi$ and $S_\ell v=2\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\,g(\nabla\psi,\nabla v)$. Hence $B=B_{\rm quad}+B_{\rm mix}+B_0$, where
\begin{align*}
B_{\rm quad}&=\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\bigl(G(\nabla v)\nabla\psi-2g(\nabla\psi,\nabla v)\nabla v\bigr),\\
B_{\rm mix}&=-\sigma\Upsilon\,v\nabla v,\\
B_0&=-\bigl(\sigma^3\zeta^3\tilde\psi^3G(\nabla\psi)+\sigma^2\zeta^3\delta\tilde\psi^2\bigr)v^2\nabla\psi+\tfrac\sigma2v^2\nabla\Upsilon .
\end{align*}
The vector $\nabla\psi$ is timelike and $\nabla f=-L$ is null, and both are past-directed (Lemma~\ref{lem_monotone}(c)). Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq_psi_f}
g(\nabla\psi,\nabla f)<0\qquad\text{on }\overlineM .
\end{equation}

On the null boundary $\mathcal H\cap\overlineM$ we use $\langle Z,d\varphi\rangle=g(Z,\nabla f)$. The terms coming from $B_0$ and $B_{\rm mix}$ are easy. The main term comes from $B_{\rm quad}$, and requires Lemma~\ref{lem_algebra}.

We start with the two easy terms. Since $G(\nabla\psi)<0$, \eqref{eq_psi_f} gives $G(\nabla\psi)g(\nabla\psi,\nabla f)\ge c$ on $\overlineM$. The other terms in $B_0$ carry at most $\sigma^2$, so
\[
-\langle B_0,d\varphi\rangle=\sigma^3\zeta^3\tilde\psi^3\,G(\nabla\psi)g(\nabla\psi,\nabla f)\,v^2+O(\sigma^2)v^2\ge c\sigma^3v^2-C\sigma^2v^2 .
\]
Since $g(\nabla v,\nabla f)=-Lv$,
\[
|\langle B_{\rm mix},d\varphi\rangle|=\sigma|\Upsilon||v||Lv|\le C\sigma^2v^2+C(Lv)^2 .
\]

We now turn to the main term. We have
\[
-\langle B_{\rm quad},d\varphi\rangle=\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\,\Phi(\nabla v),
\qquad
\Phi(Z)=2g(Z,\nabla\psi)g(Z,\nabla f)-G(Z)\,g(\nabla\psi,\nabla f).
\]
This is the quadratic form of Lemma~\ref{lem_algebra}, with
\[
Y_1=\nabla\psi\ \text{timelike},\qquad Y_2=\nabla f=-L\ \text{null},
\]
both past-directed. Since $Y_2$ is null, $\Phi(L)=0$, so $\Phi$ does not control the component of $\nabla v$ along $L$. We write
\[
\nabla v=sL+Z',\qquad h(Z',L)=0 .
\]
Corollary~\ref{cor_algebra}, with $W=L^{\perp_h}$ and $g^+=h|_W$, gives, with a constant uniform on $\overlineM$,
\[
\Phi(\nabla v)\ge c\,|Z'|_h^2 .
\]
The component $Z'$ controls $Lv$. Since $G(L)=0$,
\[
Lv=g(\nabla v,L)=s\,G(L)+g(Z',L)=g(Z',L),\qquad\text{so}\qquad (Lv)^2\le C|Z'|_h^2 .
\]
Hence
\[
-\langle B_{\rm quad},d\varphi\rangle=\sigma\zeta\tilde\psi\,\Phi(\nabla v)\ge c\sigma|Z'|_h^2\ge c^\prime \sigma(Lv)^2 .
\]
So the main term controls the derivative of $v$ along the generators of $\mathcal H$.

Adding the three terms, for $\sigma_0$ large enough,
\[
-\langle B,d\varphi\rangle\ge c\bigl(\sigma^3v^2+\sigma(Lv)^2\bigr)\qquad\text{on }\mathcal H\cap\overlineM ,
\]
and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq_bdry_H}
-\int_{\mathcal H\cap\overlineM}\frac{\langle B,d\varphi\rangle}{|\nabla_h\varphi|_h}\,d\sigma_h\ge c\bigl(\sigma^3|v|^2_{\mathcal H}+\sigma|Lv|^2_{\mathcal H}\bigr).
\end{equation}

On the lateral boundary $\Gamma$, which has no causal type, we only bound absolute values. Since $|\nu|_h=1$, the decomposition of $B$ gives, for $\sigma\ge1$,
\[
|h(B,\nu)|\le|B|_h\le C\bigl(\sigma^3v^2+\sigma|v||\nabla_h v|_h+\sigma|\nabla_h v|_h^2\bigr)\le C\bigl(\sigma^3v^2+\sigma|\nabla_h v|_h^2\bigr),
\]
and $|\nabla_h v|_h^2=(\partial_\nu v)^2+|\nabla_h^{\tan}v|_h^2$ on $\Gamma$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq_bdry_Gamma}
\Bigl|\int_\Gamma h(B,\nu)\,d\sigma_h^\Gamma\Bigr|\le C\bigl(\sigma^3|v|^2_\Gamma+\sigma|\partial_\nu v|^2_\Gamma+\sigma|\nabla_h^{\tan}v|^2_\Gamma\bigr).
\end{equation}


\medskip\noindent
\textbf{3. End of the proof.}
Inserting \eqref{eq_bdry_H} and \eqref{eq_bdry_Gamma} into \eqref{eq_integrated}, we get
\begin{multline}\label{eq_v_estimate}
\sigma^3\|v\|^2_Q+\sigma\|\nabla_h v\|^2_Q+\sigma^3|v|^2_{\mathcal H}+\sigma|Lv|^2_{\mathcal H}\\
\le C\|e^\ell\Box_gu\|^2_Q+C\bigl(\sigma^3|v|^2_\Gamma+\sigma|\partial_\nu v|^2_\Gamma+\sigma|\nabla_h^{\tan}v|^2_\Gamma\bigr).
\end{multline}
It remains to return to $u$ and $P$. We have
\[
e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\nabla_h u=\nabla_h v-\sigma v\,\nabla_h\tilde\psi,
\qquad
e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\Box_gu=e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}Pu-q\,v ,
\]
and similarly for $L$, $\partial_\nu$ and $\nabla_h^{\tan}$. The estimate of Theorem~\ref{thm_carleman} is obtained upon replacing $v$ by $e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}u$ in \eqref{eq_v_estimate}, using these identities and the triangle inequality, and absorbing the errors by taking $\sigma\ge\sigma_0$ with $\sigma_0$ large enough, depending on $\|q\|_{L^\infty(\overlineM)}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: In fact the proof controls the whole tangential gradient of $u$ on $\mathcal H_\tau$, and not only $Lu$. Indeed, $T\mathcal H=L^{\perp_g}$, so $dv(X)=g(Z',X)$ for every $X\in T\mathcal H$. We keep only $Lu$, since it is the only tangential derivative that enters the recovery formula of Lemma~\ref{lem_recovery}.
head: environment

label: lem_recovery
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Recovery formula

title: Proof
body_md:
Pick a function $\psi$ such that the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm_carleman} hold. One can take for instance $\psi=t_\mathsf{D}$ a temporal function given by global hyperbolicity. We apply Theorem~\ref{thm_carleman} with $\zeta=\zeta_0$ and $q=q_1$. Since $\|q_1\|_{L^\infty}\le A$, its constants depend only on $A$ and the geometry, and not on $\tau$.


Using~\eqref{eq_recovery} we can apply Theorem~\ref{thm_carleman} to $u=w_\tau|_{X_\tau}$ with $Pu=-\bar q\,v_{2,\tau}$. Dropping the bulk terms on the left and using \eqref{bound_admissible} we get
\[
\sigma^3|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}w_\tau|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}+\sigma|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}Lw_\tau|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}\le C\|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\bar q\|^2_{L^2(K)}+C E_{\tau,\sigma},
\]
where $E_{\tau,\sigma}=\sigma^3|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}w_\tau|^2_{\Gamma_\tau}+\sigma|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\partial_\nu w_\tau|^2_{\Gamma_\tau}+\sigma|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\nabla_h^{\tan}w_\tau|^2_{\Gamma_\tau}$. The pointwise estimate of Lemma~\ref{lem_recovery} yields
\[
|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\bar q|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\tau}\cap K}\le C_1\bigl(|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}Lw_\tau|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}+|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}w_\tau|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}\bigr)\le\frac{C_2}{\sigma}\Bigl(\|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\bar q\|^2_{L^2(K)}+ E_{\tau,\sigma}\Bigr).
\]
Recall that $f(K) \subset[\tau_a,\tau_b]$. We can now integrate over the leaves $\mathcal H_\tau$ using the coarea formula (see for instance~\cite[Section 3.4]{evans2015}). We find
\begin{align*}
\|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\bar q\|^2_{L^2(K)}&=\int_{\tau_a}^{\tau_b}\!\!\int_{\mathcal{H}_{\tau}\cap K}\frac{e^{2\sigma\tilde\psi}|\bar q|^2}{|\nabla_hf|_h}\,d\sigma_h\,d\tau\le C \int_{\tau_a}^{\tau_b}|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\bar q|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\tau}\cap K}\,d\tau\\
&\le\frac{C}{\sigma}\|e^{\sigma\tilde\psi}\bar q\|^2_{L^2(K)}+\frac{C}{\sigma}\int_{\tau_a}^{\tau_b}E_{\tau,\sigma}\,d\tau .
\end{align*}
We now fix $\sigma=\sigma_1$ large enough to absorb the first term. We then have $E_{\tau,\sigma_1}\le\sigma_1^3e^{2\sigma_1\tilde\psi_+}E_\tau$ with $\tilde\psi_+=\max_{\overlineM}\tilde\psi$, and $e^{2\sigma_1\tilde\psi}\ge e^{2\sigma_1\tilde\psi_-}$ on $K$ with $\tilde\psi_-=\min_K\tilde\psi$. Hence
\[
\|q_1-q_2\|^2_{L^2(K)}\le C ^2\int_{\tau_a}^{\tau_b}E_\tau\,d\tau=C^2\,\mathcal E^2,
\]
and the theorem is proved.
head: environment

label: rem_weight
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem_weight}
The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm_main} uses only the properties of $\psi$ required in Theorem~\ref{thm_carleman}: $d\psi$ is timelike and $\psi$ increases along future-directed timelike curves. Besides the constants of Theorem~\ref{thm_carleman}, the weight enters the final constant only through the factor $e^{2\sigma_1(\tilde\psi_+-\tilde\psi_-)}$, which is finite since $\overlineM$ is compact. No further property of the weight is needed. This is in sharp contrast with the usual applications of Carleman estimates in which the weight must be chosen carefully. This is another manifestation of the fact that, in spirit, Theorem~\ref{thm_carleman} is closer to an energy estimate than to a typical Carleman estimate (see Remark~\ref{rem_powers}).

label: lem_exterior_source
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem_exterior_source}
There is $\chi$ satisfying Assumption~\ref{assumption_sources} with $\operatorname{supp}\chi\cap\overlineM=\emptyset$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $\Phi_s$ be the flow of $L$ on $\mathsf{D}_\gamma$. Recall that the generator through $x\in\mathsf{D}_\gamma$ emanates from $\gamma(f(x))$. So $\Phi_s(x)$ tends to $\gamma(f(x))$ as $s$ decreases. Let $\mathcal N$ be an open neighbourhood of $\gamma(I)$ with $\overline{\mathcal N}\cap\overlineM=\emptyset$. For $x\in K$ there is $s_x<0$ with $y_x:=\Phi_{s_x}(x)\in\mathcal N\setminus\gamma(I)$. Choose $b_x\in C^\infty_c(\mathcal N\setminus\gamma(I))$, $b_x\ge0$, with $b_x(y_x)>0$. By continuity of the flow, $b_x(\Phi_{s_x}(x'))>0$ for $x'$ in a neighbourhood $O_x$ of $x$. Cover $K$ by $O_{x_1},\dots,O_{x_m}$ and set $\chi=\sum_ib_{x_i}$.
head: environment

label: lem_gluing
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem_gluing}
Let $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$, $\operatorname{supp} q_j\subset K$, with $\mathcal C_{q_1}(M)\subset\mathcal C_{q_2}(M)$. Let $F\in\mathcal E'(\mathsf{D})$ with $\operatorname{supp} F\cap\overlineM=\emptyset$, and let $U_j\in\mathcal D'(\mathsf{D})$ solve $(\Box_g+q_j)U_j=F$ in $\mathsf{D}$ with $\operatorname{supp} U_j\subset J^+(\operatorname{supp} F)$. Then $U_1=U_2$ in $\mathsf{D}\setminus\overlineM$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume first that $F\in C^\infty_c(\mathsf{D}\setminus\overlineM)$. Then $U_1\in C^\infty(\mathsf{D})$ and $(\Box_g+q_1)U_1=0$ in $M$. By assumption, there is $u_2\in C^\infty(\overlineM)$ with $(\Box_g+q_2)u_2=0$ in $M$ and the same Cauchy data as $U_1$, that is, $u_2=U_1$ and $du_2=dU_1$ on $\partialM$. Let
\[
\tilde U=\begin{cases}u_2&\text{in }\overlineM,\\ U_1&\text{in }\mathsf{D}\setminus\overlineM.\end{cases}
\]
Then $\tilde U\in C^1(\mathsf{D})$, and since $q_1=q_2$ outside $K$, Green's formula on both sides of $\partialM$ gives
\[
(\Box_g+q_2)\tilde U=F\qquad\text{in }\mathsf{D} .
\]
So $\tilde U-U_2$ solves the homogeneous equation and is supported in $\overlineM\cup J^+(\operatorname{supp} F)$. Since a Cauchy temporal function $t_\mathsf{D}$ of $\mathsf{D}$ increases along future-directed causal curves, $\tilde U-U_2$ vanishes in $\{t_\mathsf{D}<\min_{\overlineM\cup\operatorname{supp} F}t_\mathsf{D}\}$. Hence $\tilde U=U_2$ by uniqueness of the Cauchy problem and $U_1=U_2$ in $\mathsf{D}\setminus\overlineM$.

The case $F \in \mathcal E'(\mathsf{D})$ follows by approximation by functions in $C^\infty_c(\mathsf{D}\setminus\overlineM)$ and by using the continuity of the solution operator.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a null-cone extension $(\mathcal{M},\tilde g)$ of $(M,g)$, with $K=\operatorname{supp} q_1\cup\operatorname{supp} q_2$, write $g$ for $\tilde g$, and extend $q_1,q_2$ by zero. Both $q_j$ are admissible for $A=\max_j\|q_j\|_{C^k}$. Choose $\chi$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem_exterior_source}, and let $\tau\in\mathcal R$. Lemma~\ref{lem_gluing} with $F=\chi\,\delta'(\varphi_\tau)$ gives $V_{q_1,\tau}=V_{q_2,\tau}$ in $\mathsf{D}\setminus\overlineM$. Since $V_{q_j,\tau}=v_{j,\tau}$ on $Q_\tau$ by \eqref{eq:main},
\[
w_\tau=0\qquad\text{on }Q_\tau\setminus\overlineM,
\]
and, by continuity, $w_\tau$ and $dw_\tau$ vanish on $\Gamma_\tau$ (Figure~\ref{fig:gamma_density}), which means $E_\tau=0$. This holds for every $\tau\in\mathcal R$, so $\mathcal E=0$, and Theorem~\ref{thm_main} gives $q_1=q_2$.

label: lem_aux_riem_metric
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem_aux_riem_metric}
Let $(\mathcal{M},g)$ be a Lorentzian manifold and let $t : \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a smooth time function such that $\nabla t$ is everywhere timelike.
Define the symmetric $2$-tensor
\[
h(u,v) = g(u,v) + 2\, g(u, T) g(v, T),
\quad \text{where } T = \frac{\nabla t}{\sqrt{-g(\nabla t,\nabla t)}}.
\]
Then $h$ is a Riemannian metric on $\mathcal{M}$. Moreover, the density function associated to $h$ is the same as the density of $g$, that is $d V_h=d V_g=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ij})|}\, dx^0 \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $p \in \mathcal{M}$. Since $T$ is timelike we have a direct sum
\[
T_p \mathcal{M} = \mathrm{span}\{T\} \oplus  T^\perp.
\]
We can now choose a $g$-orthonormal frame $\{T, e_1, \dots, e_n\}$ at $p$, so that the matrix of $g$ in this frame is
\[
(g_{ij}) = \mathrm{diag}(-1,1,\dots,1).
\]
We have $g(e_i,T)=0$ for $i \ge 1$ and
\[
h(T,T) = g(T,T) + 2 g(T,T)^2 = -1 + 2 = 1,
\]
\[
h(T,e_i) = 0,
\quad
h(e_i,e_j) = g(e_i,e_j) = \delta_{ij}.
\]
Thus the matrix of $h$ in this frame is
\[
(h_{ij}) = \mathrm{diag}(1,1,\dots,1).
\]
so $h$ is positive definite and therefore a Riemannian metric.
This proves the lemma, since both properties are independent of the choice of frame.

label: lem:ultrastatic-foliation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:ultrastatic-foliation}
Let $(N,h)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and $x_0\in N$ a point
at which $\exp_{x_0}\colon T_{x_0}N\to N$ is a diffeomorphism.
Consider the ultrastatic spacetime $(\mathcal{M},g)=(\mathbb{R}\times N,-dt^2+h)$
and let $K\subsetM\subset\mathcal{M}$, with $K$ compact and $M$ open with compact closure, such that $x_0\notin\pi_N(\overlineM)$,
where $\pi_N\colon\mathbb{R}\times N\to N$ is the spatial projection.
Then Assumption~\ref{assumption_null_cone_foliation} is satisfied with
$\gamma(\tau)=(\tau,x_0)$ and $f(t,x)=t-d_h(x_0,x)$.
head: environment
name: Null-cone foliation in the ultrastatic case

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\overlineM$ is compact, we may choose
$t_-<t_+$ such that $\overlineM\subset\mathsf{D}:=I^+(p_-)\cap I^-(p_+)$ with
$p_\pm=(t_\pm,x_0)$.
The diamond can be expressed as
\[
  \mathsf{D}=\bigl\{(t,x):d_h(x_0,x)<\min(t-t_-,\,t_+-t)\bigr\}.
\]
Define $I=(t_-,t_+)$. Then $K\subsetM\Subset\mathsf{D}$, and $\overline{M}\cap\gamma(I)=\emptyset$ since $x_0\notin\pi_N(\overlineM)$. We now verify the requirements of Assumption~\ref{assumption_null_cone_foliation} for $f(t,x):=t-d_h(x_0,x)$. Since $\exp_{x_0}$ is a global diffeomorphism $d_h(x_0,\cdot)\in C^\infty(N\setminus\{x_0\})$ and $f\in C^\infty(\mathsf{D}_\gamma)$. We also have
\[
  g^{-1}(df,df)
  =-(\partial_t f)^2+|\nabla_h d_h(x_0,\cdot)|_h^2,
  =-1+1=0,
\]
since $|\nabla_h d_h(x_0,\cdot)|_h=1$ on $N\setminus\{x_0\}$. Hence, the level sets of $f$ are null hypersurfaces and they clearly foliate $\mathsf{D}$.

The description of the null cones emanating from $\gamma$ is a consequence of the expression
\[
J^+(\gamma(\tau))
=
\{(t,x):d_h(x_0,x)\leq t-\tau\}.
\]
For the inclusion ``$\subset$'', let $(t,x)\in J^+(\gamma(\tau))$ and let
$[0,1] \ni s \to \Gamma(s)=(t(s),x(s))$ be a future-directed causal curve from
$(\tau,x_0)$ to $(t,x)$. Then
\[
0\geq g(\dot\Gamma,\dot\Gamma)
=-\dot t^2+|\dot x|_h^2,
\]
and $\dot t>0$, so $|\dot x|_h\leq\dot t$. Hence
\[
d_h(x_0,x) \leq
\int_0^1 |\dot x|_h\,ds
\leq\int_0^1 \dot t\,ds
=t-\tau.
\]
Conversely, suppose that
\[
d_h(x_0,x)\leq t-\tau.
\]
By completeness of $(N,h)$, there exists a unit-speed minimizing
geodesic $\sigma:[0,L]\to N$ from $x_0$ to $x$, where
$L=d_h(x_0,x)$. Let
\[
\Gamma(s)=
\left(\tau+\frac{t-\tau}{L}s,\sigma(s)\right),
\qquad 0\leq s\leq L.
\]
Then $\Gamma$ joins $(\tau,x_0)$ to $(t,x)$ and
\[
g(\dot\Gamma,\dot\Gamma)
=-\left(\frac{t-\tau}{L}\right)^2+1\leq0,
\]
while $\dot t>0$. Thus $\Gamma$ is future-directed causal, and
$(t,x)\in J^+(\gamma(\tau))$.
head: environment

label: rem_local_ultrastatic
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem_local_ultrastatic}
Lemma~\ref{lem:ultrastatic-foliation} still holds if, for some $R>0$, $\exp_{x_0}$ is only a diffeomorphism from $\{v\in T_{x_0}N:|v|_h<R\}$ onto $B_h(x_0,R)$, provided that
\[
|t-t_c|+d_h(x_0,x)<R\qquad\text{for all }(t,x)\in\overlineM,
\]
for some $t_c\in\mathbb R$. In the proof, one takes $t_\pm=t_c\pm R$, so that $\overlineM\subset\mathsf{D}\subset\mathbb R\times B_h(x_0,R)$, and one uses that $d_h(x_0,\cdot)\in C^\infty(B_h(x_0,R)\setminus\{x_0\})$, with $|\nabla_h d_h(x_0,\cdot)|_h=1$ there. The rest of the proof is unchanged. For instance, on the round sphere $N=S^n$ one can take $R=\pi$, and the condition reads $|t-t_c|<d_h(x,x_S)$, where $x_S$ is the antipode of $x_0$: the diamond $\mathsf{D}$ must close before the null cones emanating from $\gamma$ refocus at $x_S$.
